Hooray! You helped Yebo bring the groceries home! Thank you for keeping on trying. We are proud of you!
Hello, reading explorer! Welcome to Yebo’s English reading adventure. We will read words, enjoy a story, and think about what it means. Take your time. Listening is part of learning!
Wonderful reading! You practised words, read a story, and thought about its meaning. Every little step helps you grow. Keep reading, my friend!

Read the story. You may listen to each sentence or hear the whole story.

Great thinking! You found it.
Let’s try together. Read the story again or ask for a hint.
bag
bag. A bag is something you use to carry things.
shop
shop. A shop is a place where people buy things.
help
help. To help means to do something useful or kind for someone.

Mama has given Yebo money for the shopping. First, let’s recognise a two rand coin.
Look at the value. Coins have different values. Read the number on each coin, rather than counting every coin as one rand.
Find two rand. The coin marked R2 is worth two rand. It has the same value as two one rand coins.
Mama gives Yebo 20 rand, 20 rand, 5 rand, 2 rand, 2 rand, 1 rand. Let’s count the money in small steps so he knows his shopping budget.
Count piece 1. Start with the first note. It is worth 20 rand.
Count piece 2. We have 20 rand. Add the next 20 rand. Now we have 40 rand.
Count piece 3. We have 40 rand. Add the next 5 rand. Now we have 45 rand.
Count piece 4. We have 45 rand. Add the next 2 rand. Now we have 47 rand.
Count piece 5. We have 47 rand. Add the next 2 rand. Now we have 49 rand.
Count piece 6. We have 49 rand. Add the next 1 rand. Now we have 50 rand.
Check the whole wallet. We counted every piece once. Mama gave Yebo 50 rand altogether.
Aunty Zanele bought seeds for 8 rand and a pot for 7 rand. She wants to know how much she spent altogether. Altogether tells us to add the two prices.
Start with the seeds. The seeds cost 8 rand. Start counting at 8.
Break the next price into parts. Split 7 into 2 and 5. Adding 2 first will help us reach ten.
Make ten. 8 plus 2 equals ten.
Add what is left. We still need to add 5. Ten plus 5 equals 15. Zanele spent 15 rand.
Aunty Zanele bought seeds for 6 rand and a pot for 5 rand. She wants to know how much she spent altogether. Altogether tells us to add the two prices.
Start with the seeds. The seeds cost 6 rand. Start counting at 6.
Break the next price into parts. Split 5 into 4 and 1. Adding 4 first will help us reach ten.
Make ten. 6 plus 4 equals ten.
Add what is left. We still need to add 1. Ten plus 1 equals 11. Zanele spent 11 rand.
Sipho had 20 rand and spent 6 rand on paper for the reading club. He wants to know how much is left. Spent means we take money away.
Start with Sipho’s money. Sipho starts with 20 rand.
Take away the first part. Break 6 into 5 and one. Take away 5 first. 20 minus 5 equals 15.
Take away one more. Take away the last one rand. 15 minus one equals 14.
Check by adding back. The money left, 14 rand, plus the 6 rand spent, makes the starting 20 rand. Our answer checks out.
Sipho had 10 rand and spent 3 rand on paper for the reading club. He wants to know how much is left. Spent means we take money away.
Start with Sipho’s money. Sipho starts with 10 rand.
Take away the first part. Break 3 into 2 and one. Take away 2 first. 10 minus 2 equals 8.
Take away one more. Take away the last one rand. 8 minus one equals 7.
Check by adding back. The money left, 7 rand, plus the 3 rand spent, makes the starting 10 rand. Our answer checks out.
Mr Patel has 3 bags of oranges. Each bag costs 4 rand. Each means the price is the same for every bag. We add 4 once for each bag.
Count bag 1. The first bag costs 4 rand.
Count bag 2. Add another 4 rand for bag 2. Now the total is 8 rand.
Count bag 3. Add another 4 rand for bag 3. Now the total is 12 rand.
Connect the equal groups. 3 equal groups of 4 make 12. This is multiplication. All the bags cost 12 rand.
Mr Patel has 2 bags of oranges. Each bag costs 3 rand. Each means the price is the same for every bag. We add 3 once for each bag.
Count bag 1. The first bag costs 3 rand.
Count bag 2. Add another 3 rand for bag 2. Now the total is 6 rand.
Connect the equal groups. 2 equal groups of 3 make 6. This is multiplication. All the bags cost 6 rand.

Yebo needs to pay 35 rand at the till. He can choose notes and coins from Mama’s wallet. Any payment that covers the cost is fine.
Keep the cost in view. The shopkeeper needs 35 rand for the groceries.
Build a payment. Tap one piece of money at a time. Add its value to your payment. Keep going until your payment is the same as, or greater than, the cost.
Understand the extra. If you hand over more than the cost, the shopkeeper returns the extra as change. Money you did not hand over stays in the wallet.
